subject: medicine
title: Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas: DLBCL, Follicular, and Burkitt

steps.tx: The most prevalent non-Hodgkin lymphoma worldwide presents aggressively with rapidly enlarging symptomatic lymphadenopathy or extranodal masses. Accounting for thirty to forty percent of adult lymphomas, **diffuse large b-cell lymphoma** (DLBCL) is characterized histopathologically by diffuse architectural effacement of the lymph node by sheets of large transformed B cells with prominent nucleoli. Extranodal involvement occurs in over forty percent of patients, predominantly affecting the stomach, bowel, central nervous system, and bone. Without prompt systemic chemoimmunotherapy, DLBCL is rapidly fatal within months.

steps.tx: The international standard frontline chemoimmunotherapy regimen for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma combines monoclonal anti-CD20 antibody with multiagent cytotoxic drugs. Administering the **r-chop** regimen every twenty-one days (six cycles) pairs rituximab with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin (hydroxydaunorubicin), vincristine (Oncovin), and oral prednisone. Rituximab binds surface CD20, triggering complement-dependent cytotoxicity and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis. Adding rituximab to CHOP improved complete response rates and overall survival by fifteen percent, curing over sixty percent of patients with advanced-stage DLBCL.
steps.say: The international standard frontline chemoimmunotherapy regimen for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma combines anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody with multiagent cytotoxic drugs. Administering the r-chop regimen pairs rituximab with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone. Rituximab binds surface CD20, triggering complement-mediated cytotoxicity and cellular phagocytosis. Adding rituximab to standard CHOP improved complete cure rates to over sixty percent in advanced disease.

steps.tx: The second most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma represents an indolent neoplasm arising from germinal center B lymphocytes. In **follicular lymphoma**, neoplastic lymphoid follicles comprising small cleaved centrocytes and large non-cleaved centroblasts proliferate within the lymph node cortex. The pathognomonic molecular hallmark is the reciprocal translocation t(14;18)(q32;q21), which translocates the BCL2 anti-apoptotic oncogene on chromosome 18 next to the immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) promoter on chromosome 14. Overexpressed Bcl-2 protein prevents follicular B-cell apoptosis, producing painless waxing and waning generalized lymphadenopathy.
steps.say: The second most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma represents an indolent neoplasm arising from germinal center B lymphocytes. In follicular lymphoma, neoplastic follicles composed of centrocytes and centroblasts proliferate within the lymph node. The pathognomonic hallmark is the translocation between chromosomes 14 and 18, which moves the BCL2 gene next to the immunoglobulin heavy chain promoter. Overexpressed Bcl-2 protein prevents apoptosis, producing painless waxing and waning generalized lymphadenopathy.

points: Risk of histologic transformation to DLBCL (Richter)

steps.tx: Histological transformation of an indolent low-grade lymphoma into an aggressive high-grade lymphoma carries profound clinical significance. Developing **richter transformation** or histological progression occurs in two to three percent of follicular lymphoma patients per year, where indolent follicles transform into aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Suspecting transformation is prompted by sudden explosive growth of a localized lymph node mass, new constitutional B symptoms, rising serum lactate dehydrogenase, or localized hypermetabolic foci on PET-CT with SUV exceeding fifteen, mandating repeat core needle biopsy.
steps.say: Histological transformation of an indolent low-grade lymphoma into an aggressive high-grade lymphoma carries profound clinical significance. Developing richter transformation occurs in several percent of follicular lymphoma patients annually, transforming indolent follicles into aggressive DLBCL. Suspecting transformation is prompted by sudden rapid growth of a localized nodal mass, new constitutional symptoms, rising lactate dehydrogenase, or localized hypermetabolic foci on PET-CT, requiring repeat biopsy.

steps.tx: The fastest growing human malignancy features an exceptional proliferation index approaching one hundred percent with a cell doubling time under twenty-four hours. In **burkitt lymphoma**, reciprocal chromosomal translocation t(8;14)(q24;q32) translocates the MYC proto-oncogene on chromosome 8 adjacent to the immunoglobulin heavy chain promoter on chromosome 14. Unrestrained c-Myc oncoprotein expression drives continuous cell-cycle entry and aerobic glycolysis. Subtypes include endemic African Burkitt lymphoma associated with Epstein-Barr virus presenting as massive jaw or orbital tumours, sporadic Burkitt lymphoma presenting with massive ileocecal abdominal masses, and HIV-associated disease.
steps.say: The fastest growing human malignancy features an exceptional proliferation index approaching one hundred percent with doubling times under twenty-four hours. Unrestrained c-Myc expression drives continuous cell-cycle progression. Endemic African cases associate with Epstein-Barr virus presenting as jaw tumours, whereas sporadic cases present with massive abdominal masses.

steps.tx: Microscopic examination of tissue biopsies in Burkitt lymphoma reveals an unmistakable and classic histopathological architectural pattern. High-power evaluation reveals a dense, monotonous sheet of medium-sized basophilic B cells with multiple small nucleoli interspersed with scattered pale, lipid-laden tingible-body macrophages, creating the pathognomonic **starry-sky appearance**. The macrophages contain phagocytosed apoptotic nuclear debris resulting from the rapid turnover of neoplastic cells. Immunohistochemistry demonstrates intense Ki-67 proliferation index approaching one hundred percent, surface IgM expression, CD10 and CD19 positivity, and strong nuclear c-Myc expression.

rows: Abdominal ileocecal mass, bowel obstruction, ascites

steps.tx: Aggressive high-grade B-cell lymphomas harboring concurrent translocations of both MYC and BCL2 or BCL6 oncogenes carry an exceptionally poor prognosis. Referred to as **double-hit lymphoma**, these neoplasms exhibit the morphology of DLBCL or Burkitt-like lymphoma but demonstrate extreme resistance to standard R-CHOP chemoimmunotherapy. The synergy of c-Myc driven proliferation and Bcl-2 mediated apoptosis evasion promotes rapid central nervous system dissemination and early relapse. Optimal management mandates intensive multiagent regimens like dose-adjusted EPOCH-R (etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, rituximab) and aggressive CNS prophylaxis.

steps.tx: The International Prognostic Index represents the validated clinical risk stratification tool predicting long-term survival in aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Evaluating five adverse clinical variables in the **ipi score** (mnemonic APLES: Age > 60 years, Performance status >= 2, LDH elevated above normal, Extranodal sites >= 2, and Ann Arbor Stage III or IV) divides patients into low, low-intermediate, high-intermediate, and high-risk groups. Patients with zero or one factor achieve over eighty-five percent five-year overall survival, whereas four or five factors predict a survival below fifty percent.
steps.say: The International Prognostic Index represents the validated clinical risk stratification tool predicting long-term survival in aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Evaluating five adverse clinical variables in the IPI score divides patients into four distinct risk categories. The five variables comprise age over sixty, poor performance status, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, multiple extranodal sites, and stage three or four disease, guiding decisions regarding chemotherapy intensity.
